quiz.q: Lift is proportional to…
quiz.why: Through dynamic pressure ½ρV².

quiz.q: Doubling wing area at the same speed and C_L…
quiz.why: L ∝ S.

quiz.q: Reynolds number compares…
quiz.why: ρVc/μ.

quiz.q: Induced drag is caused by…
quiz.why: Wingtip vortices tilt the lift backward.
opts: making lift with a finite wing

quiz.q: Air over the top must meet air under the bottom at the trailing edge (equal transit time).
quiz.why: It does not; the upper flow actually arrives first. NASA Glenn lists equal transit as an incorrect theory of lift.

quiz.q: Lift is only Bernoulli, or only Newton.
quiz.why: Both describe the same flow; pressure differences and flow turning go together.

quiz.q: Drag is just air friction.
quiz.why: Pressure drag and induced drag are often larger.

quiz.q: A 1,100 kg airplane with a 16.2 m² wing flies level at 55 m/s at sea level (ρ = 1.227 kg/m³). Find C_L.
With C_L,max = 1.6, find this airplane’s stall speed at sea level. Give your answer in m/s.
quiz.why: V_s ≈ 26.1 m/s (about 51 knots).

quiz.q: Find the Reynolds number of a 1.5 m chord at 55 m/s at sea level (μ = 1.789 × 10⁻⁵ kg/(m·s)). Give your answer in million.
quiz.why: Re ≈ 5.7 million.

quiz.q: Find the dynamic pressure at 230 m/s at 11 km (ρ = 0.366 kg/m³). Give your answer in Pa.
Find the drag of the Example 3.1 airplane if C_D = 0.032. Give your answer in N.
How much faster is the stall speed at 1,500 m (ρ = 1.060 kg/m³) than at sea level? Give your answer in %.
quiz.why: V_s ∝ 1/√ρ: √(1.227/1.060) = 1.076, so about 7.6% faster (≈ 28.0 m/s true airspeed).

quiz.q: Lift ∝ V², so it quadruples.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit. If speed doubles at the same C_L, how does lift change?

quiz.q: Drag is fuel. In cruise, engine thrust equals drag, so every newton of drag removed is fuel not burned and CO₂ not emitted. Needing less energy to fly is the first of NASA’s three paths to sustainable aviation.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: The same lift physics drives wind-turbine blades, which turn the wind’s aerodynamic force into clean electricity.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: A wing turns the airflow downward; by Newton’s third law the air pushes the wing up. Equivalently, faster flow over the top means lower pressure there (Bernoulli). Both describe one flow.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Dynamic pressure q = ½ρV² sets the scale of every aerodynamic force. Lift and drag coefficients C_L and C_D capture shape and angle of attack.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Lift grows with V², so halving speed needs four times the lift coefficient or wing area.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.

quiz.q: Drag comes from skin friction, pressure (form) drag and induced drag, the cost of making lift with a finite wing.
quiz.why: This is stated in the unit.
